findings.element: PT · Invoices tab · RevRec lock: disabled Invoice date select + 'Change Schedule start date instead →' escape route
findings.finding: The lock's escape route goes in a loop. The lock message says the control unlocks when Schedule start is Payment date, but after the user sets Payment date the Invoice date select is still disabled and the lock message is still shown. The locked select also always shows 'Created date', whatever the actual setting is.
findings.user_impact: A user who follows the instructions to unlock the setting comes back to the same blocked control with no explanation, so they cannot change the invoice date and may also misread their current value.
findings.suggested_fix: Base the lock state and the displayed value on the saved Schedule start and Invoice date, so that confirming Payment date enables the select and the select shows the real value.

evidence.action: In PT · RevRec lock, click 'Change Schedule start date instead →', pick Payment date in Schedule start and Confirm, then return to PT · RevRec lock.
evidence.observed: Select disabled=true and lock message visible=true, although the grey note reads 'When Schedule start is Payment date, this control can be changed.' The select is forced to 'created' regardless of the value chosen in pt-pro.

findings.element: RevRec · Schedule start confirmation modal vs Schedule details table (sub_after_release_3c1b row)
findings.finding: The modal says existing recognition schedules keep their current dates, but the existing schedule row's Schedule start changes as soon as the user clicks Confirm.
findings.user_impact: Users cannot tell what the setting really changes, which is the core of the primary task. They may believe already-recognised revenue, including closed periods, has been re-dated, or stop trusting the confirmation text.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave the Schedule start of existing schedule rows unchanged after Confirm, so the table matches the modal's 'going forward only' statement.

evidence.action: On RevRec, pick Invoice issued date in Schedule start and click Confirm (repeat with Payment date).
evidence.observed: The modal states 'Existing recognition schedules keep their current dates.' After Confirm, the sub_after_release_3c1b row's Schedule start changes from '28 Dec 2025' to '6 Jan 2026', and then to 'Payment date' on the next Confirm.

findings.element: PT · Invoices tab (and Sales tab): Invoice date / Payment posting date select vs bottom 'Update' button
findings.finding: The same tab has two save models. Changing the select saves immediately with a 'Saved' toast, while an 'Update' button on the same tab saves other changes with a 'Settings updated' toast.
findings.user_impact: Users cannot tell whether a change has already been saved or still needs Update, so they click Update again or worry that leaving the tab will lose their change.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one save model per tab: either the select saves through the tab's Update button, or the tab has no Update button when all its controls save on change.

evidence.action: In pt-pro, change Invoice date from Issued to Created, then click Update. Repeat on the Sales tab with Payment posting date.
evidence.observed: The select change shows the toast 'Saved' with no confirmation. Update then shows the toast 'Settings updated'. The Sales tab behaves the same way ('Saved' on change, plus an Update button).

findings.element: PT · Invoices tab · Pro: Invoice date row (NEW badge, help sentence, defaults caption, info callout)
findings.finding: One two-option select carries a badge and three separate text blocks. Its defaults caption says existing connections stay on Created date, but the select opens on Issued date and nothing says whether this is a new or an existing connection.
findings.user_impact: Expert users have to read three paragraphs to make a two-way choice and still can't tell whether 'Issued date' is their real saved value or a default for new connections.
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce the row to the label, the select and one short line, and remove the defaults caption, which conflicts with the value the select actually shows.

evidence.observed: The Invoice date row shows NEW, a help sentence, the caption 'New Stripe connections default to Issued date. Existing connections stay on Created date…' and a blue info callout about the transactions table. Select initial_value = 'issued'.

gaps: Sync info / transaction drilldown is not in the prototype (FDD S1.5), so how the user learns that the accounting date differs from the created date could not be checked.
No trial or new-connection variant exists, so it is unknown whether the default (Issued vs Created) is visibly communicated in those states.
'Upgrade plan' (gated Invoice date and Summary) and 'Learn more →' / 'How to change mode' links are href='#', so the gated user's forward path was never exercised.
RevRec lock was only tested from Schedule start = Payment date. Whether the lock appears or clears when Schedule start = Invoice issued date is not recorded, because the lock is a fixed variant.
'Default' / 'Invoice payment' / '+ Create additional settings' have no handlers, so per-setting-profile behaviour of Invoice date is unknown.
Escape does not close the Schedule start modal (open stays true). This was not assessed as it is keyboard mechanics owned by A11Y.

Summary gated state disables the whole select, including the pre-existing Invoice created date and Payment date. Whether that is intended depends on the FDD §2 vs S2.3 conflict, which was not resolved here.
